Subject: Post-demo qualification: measurement protocol and reproducibility checklist

Hi Asha — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed path forward so we can scope a reproducible qualification run.

Key asks you shared on the call
- Latency targets: p50/p95 for token-generation paths; initial target p95 <= 120ms for requests with 512-token output (single-stream).
- Throughput: steady-state target ~1,800 requests/min for the most common prompt bundle (see prompt set attached).
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrent active sessions ~60 (burst to 100 for short windows).
- Streaming: client requires partial-token flushes within 50ms of token emission and stable end-of-stream finalization latency.

What we (Redwood) will deliver for reproducibility
1) Measurement protocol (attached: rw-harness-manifest-v3.md) — includes sampling windows, warmup rules, and injection of KV-cache reuse scenarios.
2) Canonical prompt set (attached: BlueMatter_prompt_sample_v1.jsonl) — please confirm these represent the production mix; we'll ask you to mark any PII or scrub items before we run.
3) Environment matrix — hosted vs dedicated: we need to know whether you prefer a Redwood-hosted run (faster turnaround) or a Dedicated pool (closer to production topology).
4) Report SLA: we'll produce raw artifacts (trace logs, per-token timing), a reproducibility checklist, and a summarized performance sheet.

Immediate next steps
- Asha: confirm prompt set is representative and whether you can share the final 1k prompt bundle by Friday.
- BlueMatter procurement: please indicate whether a short on-demand Dedicated window is allowed under your existing eval MSA or if procurement needs a PO.
- Marissa/Ben: we'll pair on the measurement contract. I'll schedule a 30-min run-planning call for Thurs 10–10:30am PT.

Attachments: BlueMatter_prompt_sample_v1.jsonl (sample prompts), rw-harness-manifest-v3.md (measurement protocol draft)

Thanks — Connor

Looping in a few operational details so we keep the run reproducible and defensible for the SLOs Asha listed. Below are our proposed measurement definitions and who owns each item. Please review and flag anything missing.

Measurement definitions (proposed)
- Request definition: 1 user-level invocation = 1 request. For streaming flows we measure two things: time-to-first-token (TTFT) and token-emission delta distribution.
- Latency windows: we'll report p50/p90/p95/p99 across two buckets: short (<=128 tokens output) and long (129–512 tokens output). p95 target mapping (your ask) will apply to the long bucket.
- Throughput: measured as sustained QPS averaged over 5-minute windows after a 3-minute warmup. Bursts will be measured separately with 30s windows.
- Concurrency: active concurrent sessions measured using connection count and active-token streams; we'll log both to ensure we capture web-socket streaming semantics.

Reproducibility controls
- Seeds and non-determinism: we'll pin random seeds where possible and log model and runtime hashes. Any quantization/PEFT variants will be enumerated in the harness manifest.
- KV-cache scenarios: we'll include a cold-cache, warmed-cache, and mixed reuse profile to mimic production behavior.
- Load shaping: we'll provide JAR/recorder artifacts and a run script so BlueMatter can replay our exact traffic.

Action items (owners)
- Marissa: finalize harness manifest and run script (deliverable: rw-harness-manifest-v3.md) by EOD Friday.
- Ben: coordinate Dedicated slot procurement and cost estimate for a 2-day run (Ben will reach out to Asha with pricing).
- Connor: schedule the run-planning call and collect BlueMatter's final prompt bundle.

I'll also prepare a short appendix that maps each measurement to an artifact we will provide (traces, token timing CSVs, model hash). Connor — please confirm the Thurs 10am PT slot or propose alternatives.

Thanks — Marissa
